generation_prompts: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a polished landscape Study Buddy infographic for Analysis Reporting Lesson 1.3, titled exactly 'From evidence to Harvard referencing'. Warm white background, dark navy typography, muted teal and restrained amber accents, clear adult learning design, generous spacing. Four linked panels: '1 Read the source' with an open journal page, '2 Write in your own words' with a paragraph and pen, '3 Add an author-date citation' with exact example '(Kandel et al., 2012)', and '4 Add the full reference' with alphabetically sorted reference cards. Make the link between the author/year in the paragraph and the matching reference entry visually obvious. Three short learning callouts, exact text: 'Paraphrases need citations too', 'Check every generated reference', and 'Harvard variants differ'. Footer exact text: 'A citation points to evidence. It does not prove a claim by itself.' No fabricated quotations, DOI, source titles, page numbers, statistics, logos or fake software screenshots. The author-date example refers to a real paper but do not invent its content. Text must be accurate English and highly readable. Landscape composition.

Use case: scientific-educational. Create a landscape educational Study Buddy infographic for Analysis Reporting Task 1.3 titled exactly 'Build a 500-word overview'. Warm white, navy, muted teal and restrained amber, clean academic adult learning design matching the companion referencing guide. Main subtitle exactly 'The Data Analyst in the Workplace'. Show five paragraph cards in a clear sequence labelled '1 Role and purpose — 70 words', '2 Data preparation — 120 words', '3 Analysis and interpretation — 110 words', '4 Communication and responsibility — 130 words', '5 Conclusion — 70 words'. The five numbers sum to 500. Add a citation check panel with exactly 'At least four in-text citations' and 'Matching Harvard reference list'. A small Google Scholar search/book icon can represent research, without logos or website screenshot. Add exact footer 'Suggested structure, not an official marking scheme. Confirm how references count toward the word limit.' A small note exact text 'Read and verify your sources'. Do not imply four distinct sources are officially required. Do not include invented results, a completed essay, source metadata, quotations or fake certification. Accurate English, readable text, generous spacing.
lesson_image_final_edit_prompt: Edit this educational infographic, preserving the overall layout, palette, title, footer and three lower callouts. Correct the examples so no invented authors or unsupported source claims are displayed. In panel 2 replace the entire sample paragraph on the page with exactly '[Your accurate paraphrase]'. In panel 3 replace its sample paragraph/citation with exactly '[Your accurate paraphrase] (Surname, Year)'. Keep its instruction about adding an author-date citation, but replace the example '(Kandel et al., 2012)' with '(Surname, Year)'. In panel 4 remove ALL Anderson, Brown, Kandel, Smith names and years. Under 'References' show one highlighted generic placeholder card reading '[Surname], [Initials] ([Year])' with a second line '[Full source details]'. Other reference cards should contain only gray horizontal placeholder lines, without invented names or dates. Keep the dotted arrow connecting '(Surname, Year)' in panel 3 to the placeholder reference card in panel 4. Add a small clear label under the main title: 'Formatting placeholders — replace with verified source details'. No new names, dates, real-paper assertions, quotations, DOI, citation metadata or invented findings. The image teaches the citation-to-reference link and is not itself a completed citation example. Keep all English legible and retain the four numbered panels.
